term: eternal (ST I q.10; Lean parameter `Eternal` of `GodIsEternal`)
definition: Eternity has neither beginning nor end and is without succession, all at once (ST I q.10 a.1); it is not merely endless time. In stage 2 Eternal is a primitive predicate supplied to GodIsEternal and ClassicalAttributesSuffice.
note: ImmutableIsEternalReading states only that being in potency in no respect suffices for Eternal. It does not encode time, beginning, end or succession, so the intended sourced meaning is not a new definitionally enforced temporal theorem. The result IMMUTABLE-IS-ETERNAL-FROM-BOETHIAN-ETERNITY instantiates Eternal with the typed DEF-BOETHIAN-ETERNAL (possession of life, no beginning or end, no succession in a duration frame) and derives the sufficient condition from STMT-CHANGE-REQUIRES-POTENCY and STMT-PURE-ACT-LIVES; downstream routes, which are polymorphic in Eternal, keep the primitive parameter.
